messages:
sam: Evening handoff — quick async check (what I did / blockers / today). Short version: saw tail-latency spikes from dedicated-gpu pool A, traced to an occasional GPU OOM on a worker. Mitigations applied and latency trending down. Details below.

oncall-bot: INC created INC-2026-182 for ded-gpu-oom (severity: sev2)

sam: Timeline: ~20:15 UTC spike on p99, error rate on low-priority regen routes up ~8%. Root: a single pod OOMed and left requests queuing. Actions I took: reduced runtime batch_size via annotation, scaled replicas +2, enabled CPU-fallback route for background regen.

priya: thanks — can you paste the k8s patch/commands you ran so I can reuse in other clusters?

sam: Sure — commands I used:

```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment redwood-runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"batch-size":"4"}}}}}'
kubectl -n inference scale deploy redwood-runtime --replicas=6
```

sam: Also toggled route fallback: set route.worker_priority=low -> cpu-inference in routing-policy config for regen-* routes.

alex: I noticed PR #948 landed yesterday that bumped max_seq and changed some quant params. Could be related — is that on the canary?

sam: Yep PR #948 is on the canary pool. I triggered a canary rollback for that commit while triaging, currently rolling back to rev 42. Rollback command used: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/redwood-runtime -n inference --to-revision=42`. Can confirm canary pods are being replaced.

deploy-bot: deploy/redwood-runtime rollout status: canary -> success (2/2 pods ready)

maria: I'll monitor the canary and validate p50/p95/p99 over the next 15m. If stable I'll close the INC. Also will add a short note to the runbook about batch_size annotation.

priya: Any customer-visible impact or support tickets?

sam: No active P1s. Some 503s for background regen jobs; support ticket TKT-2211 opened to notify affected customers. We throttled those routes so paid customers unaffected.

alex: Okay I'll pick up the PR review queue and re-open #948 for fixes. First pass: ensure quant params have mem-safety checks and an e2e perf run before merge.

sam: Next steps (handoff):
- Maria: verify canary metrics and update INC (if p99 stays < 350ms for 30m, close).
- Alex: review/fix PR #948, add guard in runtime to reject batch sizes that exceed GPU mem threshold.
- Priya: FYI on rollback commands and routing toggle if you need to apply to eu-west cluster.
- Oncall: re-open INC if p99 > 400ms for > 30m or if error rate > 5% on regen.* routes.

maria: On it — will post metric snapshots and timestamped checks.

sam: Small note for next shift: watch metrics inference.gpu.mem.used (node exporter + nvml), queue.depth per pod, and runtime.annotation.batch-size. If you see repeated OOMs, consider setting global default_batch_size to 3 and file a perf regression to perf-team.

alex: I'll also add a short perf stress test in perf/e2e that runs dynamic batch-size ramps to catch these cases.

sam: handing off now. tag: @alex @priya @maria. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maria: 👍 will update INC when stable and paste a final metric snapshot.

priya: thanks — good handoff. If you want me to run the eu-west rollback let me know.

sam: not needed for now, but thanks.

oncall-bot: Reminder — if INC not closed in 4h, escalate to eng-sre lead.

deploy-bot: Note: canary rollback performed at revision 42, audit log ID: audit-4987654321
